description: The gate `verbaly check` runs in CI, as lists: missing translations, unknown keys, keys written with two texts (collisions: every place shows the first text) and translations that cannot render what the source renders. A dropped {param}, a lost rich tag or a flattened plural block is that last kind. Warnings never fail the gate and are listed too: an incomplete plural set for the locale, keys only a translation has (extra), texts the code and the source catalog disagree on (divergent: the text in the code ships) and translations written for an older source text (outdated). With drafts set, it also lists the machine translations awaiting review. Read-only. For counts use verbaly_status, to review drafts with their source text verbaly_drafts, and for setup problems verbaly_doctor.

drafts.description: Also list machine translations awaiting human review

root.description: Project root holding verbaly.config (defaults to the server working directory)

name: verbaly_missing

collisions.description: One key, several texts: every place shows the first site, so it fails the gate. Give each text its own key

divergent.description: The source catalog says one text and the code another: the code's text ships. Never fails the gate

extra.description: Keys only a translation has; files are where the code reads one, which the source language then shows as the key itself. Never fails the gate

ok.description: Whether `verbaly check` would pass (warnings never fail it)

outdated.description: Translations written for an older source text: rewrite them, or a human keeps them with verbaly review --approve. Never fails the gate

stateProblem.description: The state file could not be read, so outdated translations are not listed

title: Missing and broken translations
